To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the antitumor effect of anti-CD25 antibody is mediated through the Fc receptors, and this effect is independent of NK cells.
the antibodies that target CD25 have antitumor efficacy against ATL cells in a murine leukemia model, and that Fcγ receptors are required for the efficacy.
the therapeutic effect of the antibodies directed towards CD25 is dependent on the activation of Fc receptors in nonobese diabetes/severe combined immunoficiency (NOD/SCID) mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new therapeutic strategy for ATL. [Mol Cancer Ther 2007;6(9):2521–9]
the development of novel therapeutic strategies for ATL using antibodies directed toward CD 25.
the mechanism of the tumor-killing actions of anti-CD25 antibodies, which are currently under clinical trials for ATL and other CD25-expressing cancers.
